sources.source_name: King County Flood Warning app internal API
sources.owning_agency: King County DNRP Flood Warning Center
sources.access_method: Undocumented API called by public Next.js bundle
sources.machine_readable_availability: Yes, but only as an undocumented app backend
sources.authentication_requirements: APIM subscription key embedded in the public app bundle; no public registration path documented
sources.terms_or_usage_constraints: Unsupported integration surface. The public key should not be mirrored into project configuration.
sources.geographic_coverage: Eight county flood-system rivers; route relevance only through Issaquah Creek gauges and thresholds
sources.route_points_or_sections_covered: Issaquah Creek terminus and Lake Sammamish context
sources.available_fields: River thresholds, gauge grouping, phase numbers, gauge coordinates, last update times, short trend values
sources.update_frequency: County response updated at least once per refresh cycle; source app says every 10 minutes
sources.failure_detection_method: 500s, auth failure, or key rotation in the public app
sources.fallback_method: Use the underlying USGS and NOAA sources directly
sources.research_notes: On Wednesday, July 29, 2026, the public river list returned live JSON with Issaquah phase thresholds and grouped gauges, but the obvious direct gauge path returned a server-side failure. Because the API is undocumented and key-bound, it is unsuitable as a production dependency even though it exposes useful corroborating metadata.

sources.research_notes: Live on Wednesday, July 29, 2026: streamflow 21.5 cfs and stage 3.79 ft at 12:15 PDT. This site is about 264 m from the GPX and is the strongest direct observed route-end hydrologic signal.

sources.source_name: NOAA National Water Prediction Service - Issaquah Creek near Issaquah (ISSW1)
sources.owning_agency: NOAA National Weather Service / Office of Water Prediction
sources.geographic_coverage: Issaquah Creek near Issaquah forecast point

sources.available_fields: Gauge metadata, observed and forecast status, action/minor/moderate/major thresholds, hydrograph image URLs, stageflow arrays, ratings curve
sources.update_frequency: Observed roughly 15-minute issue times for observations and scheduled forecast issuance

sources.recommended_freshness_threshold: 30 minutes for observed status, 6 hours for forecast issue time
sources.failure_detection_method: HTTP non-200, empty JSON, stale issuedTime, or missing categories
sources.fallback_method: USGS-01 for observations; NWS-01 for alerts; ISS-01 for local phase semantics
sources.research_notes: Live on Wednesday, July 29, 2026: observed status 0.0222 kcfs / 3.8 ft at 17:15 UTC, forecast status 0.0252 kcfs / 3.8 ft at 00:00 UTC on Saturday, August 1, 2026. Official flow-based thresholds are action 1340 cfs, minor 2000, moderate 2300, major 2800.
